q: Read the temperature of cup A after 10 minutes.
Calculate how much cup B cooled in the first 15 minutes.
Describe how the rate of cooling of cup A changes over time.
It cools fastest at the start (19 °C in the first 5 minutes) and slower and slower as it gets closer to room temperature.
Both cups started at the same temperature. Explain why cup B cooled more slowly, using the idea of thermal energy.
Cup B has more mass, so it stores more thermal energy at the same temperature. It must lose more energy to fall by each degree, so its temperature drops more slowly.
Predict the temperature of both cups after a very long time.
Both reach room temperature, 25 °C: there is then no temperature difference, so no net energy transfer.
